declared.results[*].wire[0] entry fields: the recorded entry carries only name/newName (the recorder's handler threw before any validation); the replayed rename adds what a save requires before a rename is reached, as the Schedules view sends it: instructions, time and overwrite: true
declared.results[*].engineError: the error Node threw into its call route; the core's engine raises its own refusal and the wire form (wire[1].text) is what is compared
declared.results[3]: SCHEDULE_RENAME_UNCERTAIN is replayed by apps/desktop/src/main/protocol/schedule-rename-uncertain-replay.test.mjs through the K1 path that leaves a rename's outcome unknown: the channel/saveSchedule op sent, the socket cut before its answer, and the reconnected client's op/status refused, which the client library answers with opOutcomeUnknown (packages/protocol-client/src/client.ts:889; the Rust client's twin is mixdog-app-server-client/src/engine.rs:628). The desktop's capability lane turns that answer to a rename into Node's refusal (apps/desktop/src/main/protocol/capability-route.ts saveSchedule, Node: src/session-runtime/channel-config-api.mjs:63, schedule-errors.mjs scheduleRenameUncertainError), and the page text, code, name param, contextBridge property names and message are compared with Node's. Not compared for this result: wire and engineError (Node's worker-transport hop, which K1 does not have), and in sentToPage.message the cause Node's transport gave, `timeout`, which is the client's `opOutcomeUnknown` in K1 (the page shows `text`, not the message)
